units.title: All About Me and My Family

words.childMeaning: To shout happily to show you are pleased or to support someone.
practiceSentences: The whole class began to cheer for Sami.
Did you hear the crowd cheer at the match?
A loud cheer went up when Amal scored.
We cheer our team from the side of the field.
Nora gave a cheer when the rain finally stopped.

words.childMeaning: A round part that turns to make a cart or a vehicle move.
practiceSentences: The front wheel of my bicycle needs more air.
Which wheel is making that squeaking noise?
Leo watched the water wheel turn in the stream.
A cart with one broken wheel cannot roll straight.
Dad showed me how to change a wheel on the car.

words.childMeaning: Rising or falling very sharply, so it is hard to climb.
practiceSentences: The path to the top was steep and rocky.
Is that hill too steep for your bicycle?
Amal stopped halfway up the steep slope to rest.
A steep roof lets the heavy rain run off quickly.
We climbed the steep steps to the old lighthouse.

words.childMeaning: A dream is a picture or story that happens in your mind while you sleep.
practiceSentences: Amal had a happy dream last night.
What was your dream about?
Nora's dream felt very real.
I could not remember my dream this morning.
Sami wrote his strange dream in a notebook.

words.childMeaning: To stretch your arm out to get to something.
practiceSentences: Amal can reach the shelf if she stands on her toes.
Can you reach the ball under the bench?
“Reach up, then reach down to your feet,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I reach for my water bottle after every race.
Tall sunflowers reach towards the warm sunshine.

words.group: Words: how we feel and how we treat people
words.childMeaning: Not sensible, a little foolish or funny.
practiceSentences: That is a silly joke, Daniel!
Did Maya make a silly mistake in her spelling?
We laughed at the silly camel in the story.
Nobody wants to make a silly mistake in the contest.
A silly hat made everybody laugh.

words.childMeaning: A word you use to talk about doing something to or for you.
practiceSentences: I tied my shoes myself.
Should I do this myself?
Nora said, "I made this myself!"
I taught myself to ride a bike.
I will read a whole chapter book by myself.

words.childMeaning: The word used to talk about the very person you are speaking to.
practiceSentences: Did you make this cake yourself?
Take care of yourself on the trip.
Look at yourself in the mirror, Sami!
You should be proud of yourself, Nora.
Can you tell us a little about yourself?

words.childMeaning: Used to say a boy or a man did something on his own.
practiceSentences: Leo built the whole model himself.
Did Sami write the story himself?
Dad repaired the broken gate himself.
Daniel poured the juice himself.
The little boy dressed himself for school.

words.childMeaning: Used to say that a girl or woman did something without help from anyone else.
practiceSentences: Nora tied her shoes herself this morning.
Did Mina finish the drawing herself?
My mother cooked dinner herself tonight.
Amal was proud she had done it herself.
Mina wrote the invitation herself.

words.childMeaning: The very same thing that was already mentioned.
practiceSentences: The tool itself was easy to use.
Did the beach itself feel warm under their feet?
What a huge measurement, the beach itself was so long!
Sami said the answer itself was the real clue.
The door swung open by itself in the wind.

words.childMeaning: Used to say that we did something on our own.
practiceSentences: We painted the classroom ourselves.
Shall we walk to the market ourselves?
We made the decorations ourselves this year.
Amal said we could carry the boxes ourselves.
We taught ourselves a new song at break time.

words.childMeaning: Second means coming right after the first one in order.
practiceSentences: This is the second time I have visited.
Which house is the second one on the street?
Nora came second in the running race.
The second page of the book was torn.
The second road is much older.

words.childMeaning: A minute is a short amount of time, sixty seconds long.
practiceSentences: It only took a minute to finish the puzzle.
Can you hold this for just a minute?
Adam ran around the garden in under a minute.
The kettle boiled in about a minute.
The clock ticks sixty times in one minute.

words.childMeaning: A length of time that lasts sixty minutes.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin gives the class one hour for the project.
One hour of reading passes quickly with a good book.
How many minutes are in one hour?
Mum said, "Dinner will be ready in one hour."
I play outside for an hour after homework.

words.childMeaning: Early means before the usual time, near the start.
practiceSentences: In a small town near the sea, Amal woke up early.
Leo came to school early to help Teacher Yasmin.
The birds sing early in the morning.
We left early so we would not be late.
Grandpa waters the garden early every day.

words.childMeaning: In a short time from now, with not long to wait.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin says the results will arrive soon.
The bell will ring soon for break time.
Will the rain stop soon so we can play?
Adam said, "The fair is coming very soon!"
I will finish my chores soon and then read.

words.childMeaning: Past means going by something, or a time that has already gone.
practiceSentences: Amal ran past him.
“It is half past two,” said Amal to herself.
The bus went past our house.
Leo walked past the market on his way home.
In the past, people wrote letters by hand.

words.childMeaning: The time that has not happened yet, coming after today.
practiceSentences: Amal draws a picture of her future classroom.
Nobody knows the future, so we plan carefully.
What job would you like in the future?
Adam said, "In the future I will build ships."
I save my coins for the future.

words.childMeaning: An adult is a person who has grown up.
practiceSentences: An adult helps the children cross the road.
Ask an adult to read the story with you.
Every adult in the hall clapped for the class.
An adult must sign the letter from school.
Leo asked an adult for help with the heavy box.

words.childMeaning: An uncle is the brother of your mum or dad.
practiceSentences: Does your uncle live near the beach, Amal?
My uncle helped dig the holes for the trees.
Look, Theo's uncle brought a new spade!
Adam's uncle taught him how to plant seeds.
In the garden, Sami's father is planting trees with his uncle.

words.childMeaning: The child of your aunt or uncle.
practiceSentences: My cousin came to stay for the holiday.
Amal has a cousin who lives in the city.
Leo plays football with his cousin every Saturday.
Her cousin is the same age as she is.
We visit my cousin and my aunt on Fridays.

words.childMeaning: A mother or a father who looks after you.
practiceSentences: Every parent came to watch our class play.
A parent helps children learn right from wrong.
Which parent walks you to school each day?
Theo said, "My parent packed fresh fruit in my lunch."
I hug each parent before I sleep at night.

words.childMeaning: A neighbour is a person who lives near you.
practiceSentences: Who is your closest neighbour?
Amal said, "My neighbour waves every morning."
Their kind neighbour helped carry the water.
Sami is Nadia's neighbour and best friend.
Our neighbour brings us fresh eggs from her hens.

words.childMeaning: A person is one human being, like you or me.
practiceSentences: Every person in the class has a name card.
Amal is a kind person who helps her friends.
Only one person can sit on this chair.
The first person in the line opens the door.
A person needs food, water and sleep.

words.childMeaning: Feeling happy and pleased about something.
practiceSentences: Sami felt glad when his idea went into the box.
Are you glad about the vote, Maya?
I am so glad, Leo!
The whole class was glad to share their ideas.
Nora was glad to see the rain stop at last.

words.childMeaning: Having good manners and being kind to others.
practiceSentences: Nora is polite to her teachers.
Is it polite to interrupt someone?
Sami gave a polite reply to the question.
Being polite makes people feel respected.
A polite word can brighten somebody's whole day.

words.childMeaning: A promise is when you say you will really do something.
practiceSentences: Amal made a promise to water the plants.
“Let's promise something,” says Sami's mother.
Leo kept his promise to help Nora.
A promise is something you must not break.
I promise to be back before dark.

words.childMeaning: To invite someone means to ask them to come.
practiceSentences: Amal will invite her cousin to the party.
Did you invite Leo to your house?
We invite our neighbours for tea on Fridays.
Nora made cards to invite the whole class.
It is kind to invite someone who is alone.

words.childMeaning: Feeling glad for something good and wanting to say thank you.
practiceSentences: Amal felt thankful for the shade of the old tree.
What are you thankful for in nature today?
“We are thankful for the rain,” said the villagers.
I am thankful for the soil that feeds our food.
Being thankful helps us look after what we have.

words.group: Spelling: oa says the long o
words.childMeaning: To stay on top of water without sinking.
practiceSentences: My paper boat can float.
Will this stone float?
Sami, watch my boat float!
I watch a leaf float away.
Ducks float easily on the pond.

words.group: Spelling: oa says the long o
words.childMeaning: The part inside your neck that food and air pass through.
practiceSentences: A hot drink helped Amal's sore throat.
Does your throat hurt when you swallow?
Sami cleared his throat before he began to read.
The doctor asked Leo to open wide and show his throat.
Cold air can make your throat feel dry.

words.group: Spelling: oa says the long o
words.childMeaning: A person who trains a team and helps them play better.
practiceSentences: Our coach showed us how to pass the ball.
Is the coach coming to the match on Friday?
The coach praised Nora for trying so hard.
A good coach helps every player improve.
Sami thanked the coach after the game.

words.group: Spelling: oa says the long o
words.childMeaning: Bread that has been cooked until it is brown and crisp.
practiceSentences: Amal had toast and honey for breakfast.
Would you like your toast with butter?
The smell of warm toast filled the kitchen.
Leo burnt the toast and had to start again.
Two slices of toast are enough for me.

words.childMeaning: A small book of blank pages for writing things down.
practiceSentences: Sami writes the date at the top of his notebook.
Have you filled your whole notebook already?
Nora keeps a notebook for her best ideas.
My notebook has a red cover and thin lines.
Write the answer neatly in your notebook.

words.childMeaning: A book with exercises in it for you to complete.
practiceSentences: Open your workbook at page twelve, please.
Did you finish the workbook page last night?
Amal's workbook was full of neat handwriting.
We do one workbook exercise every morning.
Leo left his workbook on the classroom shelf.

words.childMeaning: A machine that takes photographs or films moving pictures.
practiceSentences: Leo pointed the camera at the tall tree.
Whose camera is this on the desk?
The camera caught Amal in the middle of a laugh.
A camera needs good light to work well.
Sami borrowed a camera for the school trip.

words.childMeaning: A machine that plays sound sent through the air.
practiceSentences: Grandma listens to the radio every morning.
Can you turn the radio down a little?
The radio said heavy rain was coming.
We heard our teacher speak on the radio.
A radio needs no pictures, only sound.

words.childMeaning: A machine that shows moving pictures with sound.
practiceSentences: The football match is on television tonight.
How long do you watch television each day?
Amal saw a programme about whales on television.
Turn the television off before you go out.
Our television sits in the corner of the room.

words.childMeaning: A huge network that joins computers all over the world.
practiceSentences: We used the internet to find facts about Kenya.
Is the internet working in the library today?
The internet lets Amal write to her cousin.
Ask a grown-up before you use the internet.
Sami found the answer on the internet in seconds.

words.childMeaning: A message you send to somebody through a computer.
practiceSentences: Amal sent an email to her aunt in Nairobi.
Did you read the email from Teacher Yasmin?
An email arrives in seconds, not days.
Leo wrote a polite email to the museum.
Check your email for the trip letter.

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: Used to say that you and the others did something on your own.
practiceSentences: You made these cards yourselves!
Did you build the model yourselves?
Help yourselves to the fruit, children.
You should all be proud of yourselves.
Look at yourselves in the big mirror.

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: Used to say that people did something on their own.
practiceSentences: The children tidied the room themselves.
Did they write the play themselves?
Nora and Leo made the poster themselves.
They taught themselves a new song.
Ducks clean themselves in the pond.

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: A person who is not named or known.
practiceSentences: Amal is kind when someone is tired or busy.
Have you ever helped someone in trouble?
Sami, is someone knocking at the door?
Someone left flowers on the teacher's desk.
Someone must lock the classroom door.

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: Any person at all, no matter who.
practiceSentences: Mum asks if anyone needs help at home.
Does anyone know the answer?
Nora, has anyone seen my pencil?
Nobody wanted to disturb anyone during the quiet time.
Can anyone here speak Swahili?

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: Every single person in a group.
practiceSentences: Everyone in our class enjoys the library.
Is everyone ready to start?
Everyone clapped when Amal finished reading.
The teacher thanked everyone for helping.
Everyone brought a small gift for Mina.

words.group: Words that stand for people and things
words.childMeaning: Not one single person.
practiceSentences: Nobody was waiting at the gate.
Why did nobody answer the question?
Nobody knew the answer except Leo.
There was nobody left in the classroom.
Nobody in Grade 3 had seen the sea before.

words.childMeaning: A person who helps keep people safe and makes sure rules are followed.
practiceSentences: An officer stands at the crossing to slow the traffic.
An officer keeps the streets safe for everyone.
Where does the traffic officer stand each morning?
Nora said, "The officer helped the lost little boy."
I waved to the officer near the market.

words.childMeaning: A person who puts out fires and rescues people from danger.
practiceSentences: Two firefighters ran towards the smoke while everybody else moved back.
How long does a firefighter train before the first day at work?
“Stand well back, please,” the firefighter said to the crowd.
My cousin Noah wants to be a firefighter when he grows up.
A firefighter visited our class and showed us the fire engine hose.

words.childMeaning: A person who owns or looks after a small shop.
practiceSentences: The shopkeeper sold fruit and bread.
Do you know the shopkeeper's name?
The shopkeeper smiled at Nora, so kind!
We waved to the friendly shopkeeper.
The shopkeeper counted the coins carefully.

words.childMeaning: A baker is a person who makes bread and cakes.
practiceSentences: The baker starts work before the sun comes up.
Our baker makes fresh bread every morning.
Amal watched the baker shape the dough.
The baker gave Leo a warm bun.
A baker needs flour, water and a hot oven.

words.childMeaning: A worker is a person who does a job.
practiceSentences: Every worker at the market wears an apron.
The worker fixed the broken gate.
Each worker helps to keep our street clean.
A worker came to mend the school roof.
The workers stopped for lunch at noon.

words.childMeaning: A leader is a person who helps a group decide what to do.
practiceSentences: Nora was the leader of the green team.
A good leader listens to everyone.
The leader showed the class where to line up.
Amal was chosen as leader for the day.
Every group needs a leader to help them start.

words.childMeaning: A team is a group of people who work together.
practiceSentences: Her team was cheering.
The green team had won!
Theo was in the red team.
Every team needs someone to carry the flag.
Amal was the last runner for the green team.

words.childMeaning: A group is a number of people or things together.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin walked between the tables, watching every group work.
A group of birds landed on the wall.
Our group made a poster about insects.
Sit with your group and share the pens.
The group walked to the park together.

words.childMeaning: A small group of homes in the countryside, smaller than a town.
practiceSentences: Amal walks past green farms on her way through the village.
The village has one school and a small library.
How far is the village from the city?
Sami said, "Everyone knows everyone in our village."
I love the quiet nights in my grandmother's village.

words.childMeaning: To meet means to come together with someone in the same place.
practiceSentences: Meet me by the school gate at eight o'clock.
Will you meet your cousin at the college?
Amal hopes to meet a sailor by the sea one day.
The friends meet at the same stall every week.
"Maybe one day I will see the sea and meet a sailor," she said.

words.childMeaning: To visit means to go and see a person or a place.
practiceSentences: Doctor Sarah will visit our class to talk about teeth.
Our class will visit the fire station on Tuesday.
You can visit mine any time, I told him.
“Grandma Hana will visit us tomorrow,” she said.
We visit the library every Saturday.

words.childMeaning: To join means to put things together, or to come into a group.
practiceSentences: The thorax is the middle part, where the legs and wings join on.
Leo wanted to join the football team.
Join the two pieces of paper with glue.
Come and join us at the table.
Nora will join the class after lunch.

words.childMeaning: The way things are arranged, one after another.
practiceSentences: Put the pictures in the right order.
The days of the week have an order.
Amal read the steps in order.
Our names are in order from A to Z.
Leo mixed up the order of the cards.

words.childMeaning: To pass means to go by, or to hand something to someone.
practiceSentences: Please pass the water to Nora.
We pass the market on the way to school.
Leo will pass the ball to Theo.
Amal passed her friend in the corridor.
Pass the pencil to the person beside you.

words.childMeaning: Send means to make something travel or go to a place.
practiceSentences: I will send a letter to my cousin.
Teacher Yasmin will send the list home today.
Amal wants to send a card to Grandma.
Send the ball across the field to Leo.
We send photographs to our family far away.

words.childMeaning: To borrow means to take something and give it back later.
practiceSentences: May I borrow your rubber, please?
Amal went to borrow a book from the library.
Leo asked to borrow a pencil.
You can borrow my coat if you are cold.
We borrow tools from our neighbour.

words.childMeaning: Practise means to do something again and again so you get better at it.
practiceSentences: Did you practise out loud three times?
Amal will practise her speech tonight.
Practise every day, and you will improve!
We practise our spelling every morning.
Leo needs to practise before the race.

words.childMeaning: To have the same opinion as someone else.
practiceSentences: Sami and Leo agree that their brothers are amazing.
Do you agree with Teacher Yasmin's idea?
I completely agree with you!
Amal did not agree at first, but then she smiled.
We all agree that the garden needs more water.

words.childMeaning: Helpful means ready to help other people.
practiceSentences: Page two showed a helpful neighbour.
Amal is helpful when the class tidies up.
Thank you for that helpful answer.
A helpful sign showed us the way.
Leo was helpful and carried the heavy box.

words.childMeaning: Happy to talk to people and play with them.
practiceSentences: Nora spoke in a friendly voice to the hurt boy.
Are the pupils friendly at your new school?
“Be friendly to anybody who looks lost,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I try to be friendly to every new pupil in our class.
Nadia the bus driver is friendly, and she waves each morning.

words.childMeaning: Mattering a great deal and needing your care or attention.
practiceSentences: Is spelling important for writing well?
Teacher Yasmin said trying hard is important.
This is an important letter for my mother.
Amal knew the contest was important to her group.
Drinking water is important on a hot day.

words.childMeaning: The surface of the earth that you walk on.
practiceSentences: Amal picked the books up off the ground.
Is the ground wet after the rain?
Nora sat on the ground to tie her shoe.
Leaves covered the ground near the school gate.
The books and pencils spilled across the ground.

words.childMeaning: Shaped like a circle or a ball.
practiceSentences: The round stone rolled down the path.
Is that ball perfectly round?
Look at that big round pumpkin!
We drew a round face on the paper.
Nora cut the paper into a round shape.

words.childMeaning: To hit something hard, again and again.
practiceSentences: Waves pound the rocks during a storm.
Did you hear the rain pound on the roof?
Leo began to pound the drum with both hands.
The workers pound the metal until it is flat.
I could feel my heart pound before the race.

words.childMeaning: To say something in a very loud voice.
practiceSentences: Why does Leo always shout when he plays football?
Did you shout for help, Nora?
Don't shout, Sami, I can hear you!
We should never shout at each other.
A sudden shout made everyone turn round.

words.childMeaning: A round golden hat that a king or queen wears.
practiceSentences: The king wore a heavy gold crown.
Who made the paper crown for the play?
A crown sparkled on the queen's head.
Amal drew a crown with seven points.
The crown was kept safe inside a glass case.

words.childMeaning: The day, month and year written down together.
practiceSentences: What date is the maths test this week?
Nora forgot to write the date in her notebook.
Every page needs a date in the corner!
The tutor checked the date before starting the lesson.
Write today's date at the top of the page.

words.childMeaning: One of two equal parts of something.
practiceSentences: Amal ate half of the mango.
Can you give me half of your pencil?
Wow, Theo, you finished half the map already!
Half the class visited the court.
Half of the class chose the library.

words.childMeaning: Coming after the first and second in order.
practiceSentences: Sami finished the third question before everyone else.
Is this the third clue in the challenge?
What a tricky third step that was!
Amal checked the third item on her list.
This is the third rainy day in a row.

words.childMeaning: At a later time, after something has happened.
practiceSentences: Amal helps with the toys, and afterwards she reads.
What did you do afterwards?
Sami, did you feel better afterwards?
The rain stopped, and afterwards the sun came out.
We ate our lunch first and played afterwards.

words.childMeaning: Before something happens, and in good time.
practiceSentences: Pack your bag beforehand so you are ready.
Did you read the questions beforehand?
Amal practised her poem beforehand.
We booked the tickets beforehand.
Thinking beforehand saves time later.

words.childMeaning: At the same time as something else is happening.
practiceSentences: Amal cooked; meanwhile, Sami laid the table.
Meanwhile, the rain grew heavier outside.
Nora read her book; meanwhile the bus waited.
Meanwhile, the class tidied the reading corner.
Leo sang, and meanwhile the drum kept time.

words.childMeaning: Finally means at last, after a long time of waiting.
practiceSentences: Finally, it was contest day.
Did the bell finally ring for lunch?
Finally, we won the prize!
Daniel finally found his missing pen.
We finally celebrated with cold juice on the grass.

words.childMeaning: The word you use to give your first reason or step.
practiceSentences: Firstly, wash your hands before you cook.
Firstly, we packed the bags for the trip.
Firstly, read the question very carefully.
Firstly, Amal said that she was sorry.
Firstly, write the date at the top.

words.childMeaning: The word you use to give your second reason or step.
practiceSentences: Secondly, add the flour to the bowl.
Secondly, we checked every spelling.
Secondly, the path was far too steep.
Secondly, Nora explained why she was late.
Secondly, turn the page and read on.

words.childMeaning: To climb means to go up something using your hands and feet.
practiceSentences: To get up, I climb a wooden ladder.
Leo likes to climb the big tree.
The snail began to climb the wall.
We climb the stairs to our classroom.
Can you climb to the top of the hill?

words.childMeaning: To let something fall, by accident or on purpose.
practiceSentences: Amal saw a girl drop her bag.
Did you drop your pencil?
Please do not drop the plates, Sami.
Nora watched the leaf drop from the tree.
Try not to drop the eggs on the way home.

words.childMeaning: To break means to make something come apart in pieces.
practiceSentences: Be careful, or the glass will break.
Do not break the chalk in half.
The old branch began to break.
Leo did not mean to break the cup.
Do not lean on the fence or it will break.

words.childMeaning: To wake means to stop sleeping and open your eyes.
practiceSentences: What time do you wake on schooldays?
Sami said, "I wake before the sun comes up."
We wake to the sound of birds singing.
Amal and Nora wake at the same time.
The alarm will wake Leo at seven o'clock.

words.childMeaning: To win means to come first or do the best in a game or race.
practiceSentences: Do you think the red team will win?
Leo and Sami want to win together.
We can win, Theo!
We tried our best to win the game.
You do not have to win to have fun.

words.childMeaning: Strong and well, because you eat good food and stay active.
practiceSentences: Sami eats a healthy breakfast every morning.
Is this soup healthy for us?
Nora, drink your milk, it is healthy!
A healthy body needs plenty of sleep.
Fresh fruit keeps our bodies healthy and strong.

words.childMeaning: Weak means not strong.
practiceSentences: The kitten was too weak to stand.
That branch is weak and might break.
Leo felt weak after his illness.
A weak wind moved the leaves a little.
The old rope was thin and weak.

words.childMeaning: Having the skill or the strength to do something.
practiceSentences: Maya is able to swim right across the pool.
Are you able to reach the top shelf?
“I am able to ride without help now,” said Sami.
I am able to spell every Unit 6 word correctly.
Karim is able to clean the highest windows safely.

words.childMeaning: Living and growing, and not dead.
practiceSentences: The seed we planted is alive and growing fast.
Is that beetle alive, or is it only sleeping?
“Every plant in this garden is alive,” said Grandma Hana.
I feel more alive when I run in the fresh air.
Amal said she felt alive after making a new friend.

words.childMeaning: Awake means not asleep, with your eyes open.
practiceSentences: Are you awake yet, Sami?
Amal stayed awake to finish her story.
The whole street was finally awake by seven.
Grandma Hana is always awake before the sun.
The baby stayed awake during the whole trip.

words.childMeaning: If you are asleep, you are sleeping and not awake.
practiceSentences: Nora fell asleep feeling calmer than before.
Is your little brother asleep yet?
Sami stayed asleep through the whole storm.
He was fast asleep before eight o'clock!
The cat fell asleep in the warm sunshine.

words.childMeaning: Weighing a lot and hard to lift or carry.
practiceSentences: That bag looks too heavy for you.
Is the basket heavy or light?
Careful, this box is heavy!
Adam carried the heavy stones to the wall.
She was friendly to the girl who dropped her heavy bag.

words.childMeaning: Moving your body on purpose to keep it fit and strong.
practiceSentences: Amal does ten minutes of exercise before breakfast.
What is your favourite exercise at school?
“Let us start with a gentle exercise,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I exercise with my brother Adam every Saturday morning.
Swimming is exercise that uses your arms and your legs.

words.childMeaning: Something a doctor or nurse gives you to help you feel better when you are ill.
practiceSentences: Doctor Sarah gave Theo some medicine for his cough.
Do you take medicine when you are ill?
Careful, Nora, that medicine is only for grown-ups!
The medicine tasted sweet, not bitter.
Each room had beds, medicine and smiling workers.

words.childMeaning: Danger means that something might hurt you.
practiceSentences: The sign warns us of danger ahead.
Leila teaches children about danger near roads.
There is no danger if you stay behind the line.
Amal knew the deep water was a danger.
Firefighters walk towards danger to help us.

words.childMeaning: To begin means to start.
practiceSentences: We begin every morning with a register.
We begin every day with a song.
Let us begin at the top of the page.
The race will begin in ten minutes.
Amal did not know how to begin her story.

words.childMeaning: To teach means to help someone learn something new.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin will teach us about insects.
Grandpa will teach Leo how to sail.
Can you teach me that game?
Amal likes to teach her cousin new words.
Books teach us about places far away.

words.childMeaning: A sound, especially one that is loud or sudden.

The whale dived beneath the cold waves.
Sami drew a whale beside a small boat.

words.childMeaning: All of something, with no part left out.
practiceSentences: Amal read the whole book in one day.
Did you eat the whole mango?
The whole class cheered loudly.
It rained for a whole week.
Sami spent the whole morning drawing.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: At any time that something happens.
practiceSentences: Come and see us whenever you like.
Whenever it rains, the path floods.
Amal smiles whenever she sees a dog.
Whenever did you find the time?
Sami helps whenever he is asked.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: In or to any place at all.
practiceSentences: Sit wherever you find a space.
Wherever Amal goes, her book goes too.
You may play wherever it is safe.
Wherever did you put my pencil?
Sami follows his brother wherever he goes.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: Any person at all, when it does not matter who.
practiceSentences: Whoever finishes first may go outside.
Give the note to whoever answers the door.
Amal will thank whoever helped her.
Whoever left this bag should collect it.
Sami plays with whoever is free.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: Whatever means anything or no matter what happens.
practiceSentences: Whatever happens, we will stay together.
Choose whatever colour you like best.
Amal will eat whatever is on her plate.
Whatever will we do if it rains!
Sami reads whatever he can find.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: Less means a smaller amount of something.
practiceSentences: The path had less wind than the beach.
Is there less shade under this tree?
There is so much less rain this year!
Sami wanted less sugar in his tea.
Use less water when you wash up.

words.group: Words that mean any one at all
words.childMeaning: Least means the smallest amount or number of something.
practiceSentences: There were at least twenty children in the hall.
Did you sleep at least eight hours last night?
At least try your best, Nora!
Amal picked at least two poems for the showcase.
Sami reads for at least an hour every evening.

words.childMeaning: Feeling very happy and eager about something.
practiceSentences: Amal was excited to share her idea in class.
Are you excited about the school play?
Sami, why are you so excited today?
The excited puppy ran in circles around the garden.
The excited fans cheered when the team scored.

words.childMeaning: Worried means feeling that something bad might happen.
practiceSentences: I felt worried about the maths test.
Why do you look so worried today?
Nadia, there is no need to feel worried!
Her worried face relaxed when she saw her mum.
Amal was worried about her lost library book.

words.childMeaning: Quiet and gentle, and not angry or excited.
practiceSentences: The sea looked calm and flat this morning.
How do you stay calm before a spelling test?
“Take one calm, deep breath first,” said Teacher Yasmin.
I feel calm when I read a book before bedtime.
Leila the firefighter stayed calm while the smoke alarm rang.

words.childMeaning: Right and equal for everyone, treating people the same way.
practiceSentences: It is not fair to take without asking.
Was the rule fair for everyone, Sami?
That is not fair, Nora!
Teacher Yasmin always tries to be fair.
A fair game gives every player the same chance.

words.childMeaning: A title is the name written at the top of a book or story.
practiceSentences: What is the title of your favourite story?
Maya read the title before she opened the book.
This title is very long!
The teacher wrote the title on the board.
"I can see words in books," said Leo, and he read the title out loud.

words.childMeaning: The beginning is the first part, before the middle and the end.
practiceSentences: Stars were beginning to appear in the sky.
Why is the film beginning so late?
This is the beginning of a new day, Amal!
The class is beginning in five minutes.
Read the beginning of the story again.

words.childMeaning: The ending is the last part of a story.
practiceSentences: The story had a happy ending.
Amal wrote a new ending for the tale.
Which ending do you like better?
The ending surprised the whole class.
Leo could not guess the ending.

words.childMeaning: A problem is something difficult that you need to think about or solve.
practiceSentences: We worked together to solve the problem.
Is the broken bike a big problem?
Nora, do not worry, that is not a problem!
The teacher explained the maths problem slowly.
Daniel solved the problem with a clever plan.

words.childMeaning: A thought or plan that comes to you in your own mind.
practiceSentences: Amal wrote her best idea on a small folded paper.
Sami had one idea, but he kept it hidden all morning.
Whose idea was the classroom reading tent?
Adam said, "I have an idea for our poster."
My best idea came while I was walking home.

words.childMeaning: Something that is true and can be checked or proven.
practiceSentences: Teacher Yasmin wrote one surprising fact about numbers on the board.
It is a fact that spiders have eight legs.
Can you share one fact about the moon?
Adam said, "A fact can be checked and proven."
My favourite fact is that octopuses have three hearts.

words.childMeaning: A message is words you send to somebody.
practiceSentences: Amal left a message for her teacher.
The message said to meet at the gate.
Leo sent a message to his cousin.
What is the message in this story?
Grandma wrote a short message on the card.

words.childMeaning: The meaning is what a word or a story is telling you.
practiceSentences: Look up the meaning of this word.
Amal explained the meaning of the poem.
The meaning was clear to everyone.
Leo asked about the meaning of the sign.
Two words can have the same meaning.

words.childMeaning: The sound a person makes when they speak or sing.
practiceSentences: Sami has a deep singing voice.
Can you use a quieter voice, please?
What a lovely voice you have, Nora!
Grandma Hana's voice always sounds warm and kind.
Amal read the poem in a clear voice.

words.childMeaning: A tale is a story, often an old one that people retell.
practiceSentences: Grandma told us a tale about a clever fox.
This tale is hundreds of years old.
Amal wrote her own tale about the sea.
The tale ends happily.
Every village has its own tale.

words.childMeaning: A way people talk and write to share ideas and feelings.
practiceSentences: Every language has its own sounds and its own writing.
Nora speaks one language at home and another at school.
Which language do you use when you talk to Grandfather?
"Sign language is beautiful to watch," said our teacher proudly.
Learning a new language takes patience, but I enjoy it.

words.childMeaning: A poem is a piece of writing with a nice rhythm or rhyme.
practiceSentences: Behind it lay a poem about her neighbour Theo.
Nadia wrote a short poem about the sea.
Read this little poem out loud: A nest is a home for a bird.
Leo learned the whole poem by heart.
Read this poem: At the zebra crossing, Look around at city places.

words.childMeaning: A question is what you ask when you want to know something.
practiceSentences: Amal asked a question about the rainbow.
“Good question,” said Teacher Yasmin.
“That is my favourite question,” said Teacher Yasmin, laughing.
Amal put her hand up to ask a question.
Every question ends with a question mark.

words.childMeaning: A sentence is a group of words that tells us something and makes sense.
practiceSentences: She fixed one sentence on her helpers page.
Write one sentence about your picture.
Every sentence begins with a capital letter.
Amal read her best sentence aloud.
That sentence needs a full stop.

words.childMeaning: Choose means to pick the one you want.
practiceSentences: Part 1: Choose your pages.
“Everybody, please choose a partner for today,” said Teacher Yasmin.
Choose a book from the shelf.
Amal could not choose between the two hats.
You may choose either the red pen or the blue one.

words.childMeaning: To choose what you will do after thinking about it.
practiceSentences: Sami could not decide which colour to use.
Will you decide before the bell rings?
Hurry and decide, Leo, the box is closing soon!
The class had to decide together.
Nadia could not decide between the two books.
